title: Early stopping loses higher-scoped fixture teardown errors
provenance: Evaluator-authored problem-only adaptation combining the public early-stop issue #11706 and same-fixture finalizer issue #12047, retrieved 2026-10-07. Not an authenticated pre-fix issue snapshot. Solution code and implementation suggestions omitted. Public historical evaluation case; not a private or contamination-free holdout.
body: When a test fails and pytest stops early because of --maxfail or --stepwise, errors raised while tearing down module-scoped or session-scoped fixtures are not reliably reported as teardown errors belonging to the last executed test. The process can abort, and reports consumed by plugins omit teardown failures. Reproduce with two tests sharing a higher-scoped yield fixture whose teardown raises: the first test fails and the second should not execute. The completed test must receive its ordinary failure report and a teardown error report; all already-active fixture finalizers must execute exactly once, including when setup rather than the test body failed, and multiple cleanup errors must remain visible. This includes multiple independently failing callbacks registered with request.addfinalizer on the same higher-scoped fixture, alongside failing finalizers on other fixtures; every callback must run exactly once and every exception must appear in the current item’s teardown report. Teardown hooks must observe that no next item will run when the session has decided to stop. Preserve ordinary fixture reuse and the existing exit behavior of --maxfail and --stepwise. A session stop/fail decision already communicated to plugins must remain set if a plugin subsequently tries to clear it, with a warning explaining the ignored attempt. Add regression tests for the stopping paths and preserved normal behavior.
